previous.title: Generative Social Science
previous.notes: Human interactions form one of the most important complex dynamic systems we know. This meeting introduces how social scientists model those interactions and explores how AI tools—including large language models, reinforcement learning, and causal graphs—could make social science more powerful and accessible.
agenda: A brief introduction to mathematical game theory: an equilibrium-based, static approach.
A brief introduction to agent-based simulation: a dynamic-systems approach.
Discussion of Epstein’s “generative manifesto” and its argument for agent-based simulation over equilibrium-centred approaches.
Gauge interest in a follow-up meeting on AI for social science.

readings.title: AI for Just Work: Constructing Diverse Imaginations of AI beyond “Replacing Humans”
readings.authors: Weina Jin, Nicholas Vincent, and Ghassan Hamarneh
readings.notes: Calls on the AI technical community to diversify its collective imaginations of AI beyond replacing humans. The paper identifies limits in the mainstream imagination of AI and demonstrates an initial method for constructing alternatives in two AI tasks.

readings.title: The Values Encoded in Machine Learning Research
readings.authors: Abeba Birhane, Pratyusha Kalluri, Dallas Card, William Agnew, Ravit Dotan, and Michelle Bao
readings.notes: Audits highly cited NeurIPS and ICML papers to identify the mainstream values guiding AI development and examines how those values can support the concentration of power.

recommendations.title: Machine Learning that Matters
recommendations.notes: Wagstaff’s 2012 ICML keynote paper argues that machine-learning research has lost touch with consequential problems in science and society. It highlights limitations in commonly used datasets and evaluation metrics, weak communication with originating domains, and the need to conduct research for greater real-world impact.
